They include the complete 4(c) condition and its pertinence exception. Separately, 4(d) requires a readable copy of pertinent upstream NOTICE attributions in at least one permitted location: a distributed NOTICE text file, accompanying Source or documentation, or a display generated by the Derivative Works if and wherever such notices normally appear. Those location choices do not displace retention within Source under 4(c). NOTICE contents are informational, and the closing paragraph preserves compliance with the License's conditions. No contrary provision was found.

limitations: Determining pertinence requires the wording and scope of each upstream notice and the material actually retained. A component name or the removal of a file alone cannot settle that question.

The assertion concerns retention within distributed Source. Section 4(c) establishes no obligation to supply Source with an Object-only package. Section 1 defines Object as a form resulting from mechanical transformation or translation of Source.
reasoning: Section 4(c) specifies both the origin and the destination of the notices. The licensee must retain in distributed derivative Source all copyright, patent, trademark and attribution notices from the Work's Source, excluding those that do not pertain to any part of the Derivative Works. A notice that pertains to even one remaining part is therefore within the requirement.
